newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rodamco positive on long-term trend.
newsitem.headline: Rodamco positive on long-term trend.

text.p: Property investment firm Rodamco NV said on Wednesday it expected the upward trend in its earnings to continue in 1997/98 and later years.
"We are positive about this year's net profit and that also goes for the years ahead," managing director Jean Kremers told a news conference.
He added that Rodamco also expected the positive revaluation of its property portfolio to continue in the coming years.
After a number of very meagre years, property markets had only recently started the cycle of revaluation gains and the scale of these gains was still fairly limited, Kremers said.
But he said the effects of changes in currency exchange rates, a third key element in Rodamco's results, were unpredictable so that the fund could not make a forecast of its total performance.
Rodamco believes the Spanish property market, where it has invested almost 10 percent of its European portfolio, is highly attractive at the moment.
"We would like to buy more well-located office buildings there, but you can hardly get them," Kremers said.
In France, he said, investments in shopping centres still offered good prospects and Rodamco believes the French offices market might also be on the path to recovery.
But in Germany, investment in offices was still seen as unattractive and the outlook for shops was mediocre.
In North America, Rodamco has benefited from its investments in so-called super-regional markets, where retail sales have outperformed general trends.
Rodamco has recently sold an office project in Boston for 530 million guilders for slightly more than its book value.
It decided to sell the office as rental income on this project had gone up substantially in recent years and the prospects for a further rise were limited.
Last year, Rodamco invested more than two billion guilders in new properties and it sold property worth 500 million, mainly in Britain and Germany.

In France, it bought the property firm Cegep for 800 million guilders and in the U.S. it swapped a 12.5 percent stake in unlisted Corporate Property Investors for a direct interest in three malls which bring in a much higher return.
In March, shortly after the end of the financial year, Rodamco bought the so-called Imry property portfolio from Barclays Plc for 775 million guilders.
Kremers said the acquisitions had just about used up Rodamco's cash reserves but he added that the group would not walk away from other attractive prospective takeover candidates.
These would be financed by selling other properties or by borrowing fresh funds. A share issue was rather unlikely, given the ample scope for borrowing funds, he added.
Earlier today, Rodamco said it expected net profits per share to show a further rise to at least 3.40 guilders in 1997/98.
In the year to February 29, 1997, Rodamco's net profit grew by 14 million guilders to 460 million guilders or 2.89 guilders per share.

After a positive property revaluation of 77 million guilders and a gain on currency rate movements of 509 million, the group posted a total full-year performance of 1.04 billion guilders, more than doubling the 435 million of 1995/96.
In the first quarter of the current financial year, net profits rose by 28 percent to 143 million guilders.
Rodamco posted a first-quarter positive property revaluation of 14 million guilders, but currency rate changes had a negative effect of 46 million in the quarter.
-- Theo Kolker, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
